I found three trailing "not X" / "rather than X" clauses in the passage.

1. "Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open." Fail-closed versus open is a security-domain distinction, so it fails the ordinary-knowledge test. I flagged it without editing, since the rule says to escalate uncertain cases.

2. "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident." This is the rule's own on purpose/by accident example, so the trailer is cut.

3. "Cybersecurity today is not merely an IT concern; it is a multidimensional discipline…" This is a "not merely X; it is Y" construction, not a trailing clause, so it is out of scope.

The phrases "rather than exploit them" and "reactive posture" are not trailing antonym clauses tacked onto a sentence, so they stay as written.
